newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka seeks Tamils' friendship for peace.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka seeks Tamils' friendship for peace.

text.p: The Sri Lankan government on Thursday took its peace campaign into the minority Tamil community's heartland when it launched a plan to rebuild an important Tamil library burned down 16 years ago.

The rebuilding of the Jaffna library, gutted by a fire alleged to have been set by police on June 1, 1981, would mark the beginning of a lasting bond between the people of the north and the south, President Chandrika Kumaratunga said.

"The rebuilding of the Jaffna library is symbolic of a new peace, a new understanding and a new harmony among the people of Sri Lanka," Kumaratunga said, launching the 700 million rupee ($12 million) programme in the capital Colombo.

Kumaratunga said the torching of the library, considered a rare storehouse of Tamil literature and an important landmark in Jaffna in northern Sri Lanka, became a rallying point for Tamil youth to join rebels fighting for a homeland in the island's north and east.
Sri Lanka is embroiled in a 13-year-old struggle with the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels, a war that the government says has killed more than 50,000 people.
Tamils, most of whom are Hindus, make up slightly more than 12 percent of Sri Lanka's population of 18 million. The mostly Buddhist Sinhalese account for 74 percent.

In a goodwill gesture, two Sinhalese students on Thursday handed over to Kumaratunga a book and a brick each, both of which would go towards the rebuilding of the Tamils' most important intellectual seat.
The library is among several institutions in the Jaffna peninsula damaged during the conflict.

Further damage was caused to the town when security forces invaded the peninsula, finally taking full control of it in April last year. The rebels have now re-established themselves just south of the peninsula.
Kumaratunga, whose government has proposed an ambitious peace plan, said the army was prepared to rehabilitate parts of the country damaged by war when the conflict was over.
The final draft of the peace plan, which envisions a new constitution and the devolution of wide-ranging powers to Tamils, is expected to be presented in parliament before November.
